batchSend.title: Batch send
batchSend.intro: One recipient per line: address, amount, optional memo. walletd packs recipients into as few proofs as consensus allows.
batchSend.invalidLine: Line {{line}} has an invalid address or amount.
batchSend.feeError: Enter a positive fee with at most 8 decimal places.
batchSend.feeNote: Automatic is recommended. The node raises a low value to the byte-proportional relay minimum; paying more does not buy a faster lane.
batchSend.custodial: Batch send needs a self-hosted walletd that holds this wallet's seed. This app will not upload your seed to enable it.

walletMaintenance.title: Notes
walletMaintenance.intro: Fewer notes make large payments cheaper and faster to prove.
walletMaintenance.warning: Do not consolidate a normal wallet just to make the count smaller: it costs a real fee and creates an on-chain transaction. It is useful for mining and payout wallets with hundreds of small matured notes.
walletMaintenance.custodial: Manual consolidation needs a self-hosted walletd that holds this wallet's seed. Automatic fee-safe consolidation remains a daemon setting; the app never uploads your seed.

mining.nodeNotReady: The ZKAS node started but its RPC is not ready yet. Keep it running and press Start mining again shortly.
mining.webIntro: The desktop app installs and supervises the nodes and Stratum bridge.
mining.webNoBackground: Browser and mobile wallets cannot run mining services in the background.
mining.title: Mine to your wallet
mining.intro: The app installs, connects, and keeps every required service running.
mining.heroText: Rewards go straight to this wallet — there is no pool account and no fee. The app installs what is missing, starts the node, and keeps it running.
mining.noDualBridge: No verified merged-mining bridge is published for this device. ZKAS-only mining remains available.
mining.setupIntro: Recommended choices are ready. Change only what you need.
mining.zkasNodeNote: Supplies work and receives solved blocks.
mining.automaticNote: Install, run, and sync on this computer.
mining.existingNodeNote: Use mining gRPC on your LAN or server.
mining.kaspaNodeNote: The parent node for the same ASIC work.
mining.kaspaAutomaticNote: Install and run Kaspa on this computer.
mining.kaspaExistingNote: Connect to a Kaspa mining gRPC endpoint.
mining.vardiffNote: Vardiff adjusts after the ASIC connects. This starting value changes share reporting, not block probability or rewards.
mining.connectIntro: Use the address that reaches this computer.
mining.lanPreferred: Preferred · try another if your ASIC uses it
mining.lanSameRouter: ASIC on the same router or VPN
mining.remoteNote: Public IP, DNS, or VPN hostname
mining.lanReady: LAN is ready automatically. For an internet ASIC, forward TCP {{port}} to this computer or use a VPN, and restrict the firewall to your miner’s IP. Never forward node RPC to the internet.
mining.startToReceive: Start mining to receive ASIC work.
mining.nodeSyncingWarning: The ZKAS node is syncing. Keep the app running; the bridge is supervised and mining becomes ready when the node catches up.
mining.cpuNote: For setup testing only; ASICs are vastly faster.
mining.chooserIntro: Pick what to mine and where the work comes from. The same ASIC hashing can be paid on one chain or two.
mining.whatToMineNote: Merged pays two chains from one ASIC.
mining.dualNote: One ASIC, both chains, paid separately.
mining.noDualBuild: No verified merged-mining build for this device — ZKAS-only is available here.
mining.payoutsNote: Rewards go straight to you; no pool account.
mining.zkasNodeChooserNote: Supplies the work and receives ZKAS blocks.
mining.kaspaNodeChooserNote: The parent chain for the same ASIC work.
mining.firstRunInstalls: First run installs: {{list}}. Verified downloads, then it starts.
mining.dashboardNote: Served by the mining bridge on this computer. It appears once mining is running.

endpointField.hint: Any node's IP and port — it does not have to be on this computer. e.g. 203.0.113.5:16110

nodeStartDialog.title: Choose how to run it
nodeStartDialog.miningNote: Smallest. Validates the chain and serves miners, but does not keep old wallet notes.
nodeStartDialog.shieldedNote: Keeps complete wallet history while pruning old full block bodies.
nodeStartDialog.archiveNote: Keeps complete wallet history and every block body. Uses the most disk.
nodeStartDialog.inboundNote: Optional. Other nodes can connect to this computer on TCP port {{port}}.
nodeStartDialog.firewallPublic: Allow inbound TCP {{port}} in the operating-system firewall. If this machine is behind a router, forward {{port}} only if you want public inbound peers.
nodeStartDialog.firewallPrivate: The node makes outbound peer connections and will sync normally. Its P2P listener stays on this device.
nodeStartDialog.rpcPrivate: Node RPC is private by default. Trusted-LAN access can be enabled in Host; never expose TCP {{port}} to the internet.
nodeStartDialog.miningConflict: This wallet currently uses the local node. Switch the wallet to its public service before running the history-free Mining mode.

nodeRunner.webNote: A phone or browser cannot safely keep a full node running. The wallet still works through its selected node.
nodeRunner.title: Your ZKAS node
nodeRunner.intro: Private wallet access and direct mining, managed by this app.
nodeRunner.installNote: The verified ZKAS release is downloaded into the app's private data folder.
nodeRunner.updateNote: {{release}} fixes fresh-node synchronization and shielded-history transfer.
nodeRunner.rpcNotReady: The process is running but RPC is not ready yet: {{error}}
nodeRunner.movingWalletToPublic: Moving wallet to the public node…
nodeRunner.walletSeparate: The wallet is separate from the node process above.
nodeRunner.localSyncing: Local node is syncing. Your wallet stays on {{source}} with its current balance until the local node is complete.
nodeRunner.fillingSynced: Synced, but still filling in shielded history from peers{{from}}. Block sync waits for this, so the block count can sit still for a while — it is working, not stuck. The wallet can attach once the node log says "shielded history: VERIFIED" (or the floor drops below your wallet's birthday). Your wallet stays on {{source}} until then.
nodeRunner.fillingSyncing: Local node is syncing and still filling in shielded history from peers{{from}}. Block sync waits for this, so the block count can sit still for a while — it is working, not stuck. The wallet can attach once the node log says "shielded history: VERIFIED" (or the floor drops below your wallet's birthday). Your wallet stays on {{source}} until then.
nodeRunner.walletNotAnswering: The wallet is open, but its selected node is not answering yet. It retries automatically and keeps the last confirmed wallet state visible.
nodeRunner.miningNeverOffered: Mining mode is never offered to the wallet because it does not retain complete historical notes.

selfHost.webIntro: Local process control belongs in the desktop app.
selfHost.webNote: The browser cannot install or supervise programs on your computer. The desktop build keeps services on loopback and restarts managed processes if they fail.
selfHost.title: Local services
selfHost.intro: Private, supervised services on this computer.
selfHost.networkIntro: Use the wallet service from another device and choose how the node participates.
selfHost.pairNote: Scan this in the ZKas wallet app — no tokens to type.
selfHost.pairingAlt: Pairing code for the ZKas wallet app
selfHost.pairingWarning: Anyone who scans this gets full access to this wallet. Treat it like the recovery seed.
selfHost.optDeviceNote: Random loopback port. Nothing else can connect.
selfHost.optLanNote: Authenticated service for desktop and mobile apps on a trusted LAN.
selfHost.optWanNote: Authenticated backend for a trusted HTTPS reverse proxy or VPN.
selfHost.lanFirewall: Allow inbound TCP {{port}} in the firewall for Private/Home networks only. The app does not change firewall rules or enable UPnP.
selfHost.wanForward: Forward the public HTTPS URL through Caddy, nginx, Tailscale, or Tor to this computer. Do not expose the plain backend port directly to the internet.
selfHost.nodeRpcLanNote: Lets another wallet or miner use TCP {{port}}. No authentication—never forward it to the internet.
selfHost.publicP2pNote: Accept peers on TCP {{port}}. This does not expose wallet data or RPC.
selfHost.stopBeforeApply: Stop the managed node before applying changed node access. Wallet-service changes do not require stopping it.
selfHost.walletEngineNote: Sync and proving API embedded in this app.
selfHost.boundNote: Bound to this device. The app token is never shown or forwarded.
selfHost.explorerNote: Local chain REST API and transaction index.
selfHost.dataApiNote: Data API, not a web page — the address itself returns 404. Try {{url}}/info/blockdag.
selfHost.lastExit: Last exit: {{exit}} — if the wallet's Explore tab still works, another copy is already serving this port. Use View logs for the exact reason.
selfHost.dataBackupNote: Wallet backups contain the irreplaceable key. Node chain data and the explorer index are intentionally not copied—they are large, public, and can be rebuilt.
selfHost.startupNote: Start the app with your computer. An encrypted wallet still opens locked.
selfHost.trayNote: Closing the window keeps active node or mining services in the tray, but immediately locks the spending engine. Use “Quit and stop services” in the tray to stop every child process.

dashboardView.liveUnavailable: Live data is temporarily unavailable. Showing the last saved snapshot.
dashboardView.notResponding: The explorer API is not responding.
dashboardView.title: Network
dashboardView.intro: Public chain facts. Payment details remain private.
dashboardView.tailNote: The schedule ends in a permanent tail emission; it has no fixed terminal supply.

transactionView.title: Transaction
transactionView.privateNote: The public chain proves this transaction is valid. It does not reveal the sender, recipient, or transferred amount.

addressView.title: Shielded address
addressView.invalid: This is not a valid-looking ZKAS address.
addressView.noPublicNote: ZKAS addresses do not have transparent explorer pages. Only the holder's viewing key can discover received notes, amounts, and transaction history.
